newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Strong demand takes Bucharest shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Strong demand takes Bucharest shares higher.

text.p: Buying pressure lifted most Bucharest shares on Monday, with prices posting more significant gains on the second tier than on the first.

"Demand from both foreign and local buyers was stronger for stocks in the lower section," said a trader. "Apparently, everyone started looking for cheaper shares. If pressure continues, they will soon not be that cheap anymore."

Prices of 29 stocks edged up, 10 moved lower and two remained unchanged by the close. Four companies had no trade and two were suspended. Buying pressure in late trading drove most closing prices higher.
The market was seen rising on Tuesday. "Mondays are always slower. Tuesday is going to be more active," a broker said.
Volume thinned to 3.7 million shares from 5.4 million last Friday in light supply and turnover dropped 6.7 billion lei ($943,000) to 20.2 billion.
Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, jumped by 3.08, 3.05 and 3.02 percent respectively from Friday.
First-tier gainers at close included Antibiotice and Terapia pharmaceuticals, which firmed 100 and 500 lei respectively to 9,300 and 13,000.

Fertiliser makers Azomures and Sofert also picked up. Azomures closed 50 stronger at 4,450 and Sofert climbed 3,000 lei to 39,500. Chemical plant Oltchim was the only decliner, shedding 100 lei to close at 5,200 under slight selling pressure in late trading.
Armatura industrial fittings maker, chemical plant Sinteza were the most heavily traded second-tier stocks.
Aurora footwear maker and Silcotub a steel pipe manufacturer were in demand, with price gains of 48 and 35 percent to 20,000 and 21,969 lei. Newcomer Amylon, a starch maker, had no trade.
